At Janauacá, it is worth waking up before breakfast. A canoe glides onto the still water, the forest gradually fills with birdsong, and intertwined branches appear in the shoreline reflections. From a small boat, the Amazon looks quite different than it does from a ship's deck: your attention is drawn to a single bird, movement at the water's edge and a narrow channel between trees.

Janauacá Lake is part of the Amazon Clipper itinerary departing from Manaus. The morning outing focuses on observing the forest and river life. Pink river dolphins inhabit the lake area, although every sighting depends on natural conditions. After returning to the vessel, the program continues with a forest walk and an introduction to local residents whose livelihoods include fishing, growing cassava and gathering forest products.

On Ada Tours' three-day cruise, Janauacá occupies a substantial part of the second day. Later, the itinerary includes piranha fishing and an evening canoe outing. Specific stops depend on water levels and navigation conditions. It is this proximity to the living river that makes the lake memorable: here travelers observe the Amazon as everyday life unfolds.

## Forest and Water in the Southern Amazon

Jardim da Amazônia Lodge is located in the São José do Rio Claro area, in the transition zone between the Amazon and the Cerrado. Here the journey continues along forest trails and waterways: trees reach the riverbanks, and a leisurely walk offers good opportunities for birdwatching.

The lodge serves as a base for discovering the surrounding nature. On the Ada Tours itinerary, a forest walk includes an introduction to local flora, fauna and the history of rubber extraction; travelers then paddle canoes along the Claro River toward Anaconda Lake. Between outings, there is time for lunch and a rest in a hammock.

This is the Amazonian part of the route through Mato Grosso. The program links it with Bom Jardim, the Chapada dos Guimarães plateau and the Northern Pantanal.
